title: Stale (ghost) entries in selected_columns inflate the toggle count, causing 'select one column' to silently revert to all-selected and pull in unrelated real columns
description: When selected_columns contains names that are no longer in the current schema (the component's own first-class 'stale ghost rows' feature, rendered with the '(not found)' suffix), those stale names still live inside `selectedColumns`. In toggleColumn's add-branch, `const next = [...selectedColumns, col]` includes the stale entries, and the all-selected revert guard `if (next.length >= allColumns.length)` compares this inflated length against `allColumns.length` (which EXCLUDES stale columns). The stale entries can push `next.length` to `>= allColumns.length` before the user has actually selected every real column, so toggling a single real column ON silently flips the node back to empty (= keep all columns), thereby selecting other real columns the user never checked and dropping the explicit list. Example: allColumns=[a,b,c], selected_columns=["a","stale1"]; user checks `b` -> next=["a","stale1","b"], length 3 >= 3 -> onUpdate('selected_columns', []) -> a,b,AND c are now kept. Column `c` was never selected by the user. The length comparison should be against the count of REAL selected columns (filtered through allColumnNames), not the raw array that includes ghosts.
evidence: Lines 57-64: `const next = [...selectedColumns, col]; if (next.length >= allColumns.length) { onUpdate('selected_columns', []) } else { onUpdate('selected_columns', next) }`. `selectedColumns` may contain stale names (staleColumns is built at lines 28-33 from exactly `selectedColumns.filter(name => !allColumnNames.has(name))`), so `next.length` over-counts relative to `allColumns.length` which is derived from availableColumns/columns with no stale entries.
